examples.role_boundary: Models provide local Boolean predictions. Shared code explores and repositions only on physically verified edges. Starting NanoJev is not untouched Qwen.

controller.prediction_cache: once per visited coordinate in a static maze
controller.selection_rule: untried p>=0.5 edges first; goal Manhattan distance, destination visits, descending p, N/E/S/W
controller.probe_rule: if all untried edges have p<0.5, physically attempt by descending p, goal Manhattan distance, destination visits, N/E/S/W
controller.reposition_rule: BFS to nearest frontier using only physically traversed open edges
controller.collision_rule: nonfatal; preserve position; mark the undirected edge blocked and never retry it
controller.fallback_definition: low-probability probes only; no full-map route or safe-action fallback
controller.memory_termination: all frontiers exhausted, goal reached, or attempt budget exhausted
controller.atomic_metric_scope: first-visit states chosen by this model-guided trajectory; not an identical cross-model audit cohort

controller.planner: actual next-step collision filter, then shortest static next-head path to current food; next body except head is blocked
controller.model_input: current physical state, action question, candidate descriptions only
controller.sample_rng: independent Python Random per episode, SHA256([episode_id, seed]) first 32 bits; one recorded draw per model decision
controller.attribution: food collection and survival use a common code planner; models choose only residual ties

examples.role_boundary: The shared code planner filters immediate collisions and ranks static food paths. Models choose only among remaining candidates. Forced moves are code decisions, not model decisions.
examples.probabilities: Conditional action probabilities over the actual planner-offered candidates; excluded directions have no model probability.

protocol.policy_selection: Maximize the smaller mean food score of NanoJev and Jev; break ties by their mean food score, then survival rate, then greedy. Apply one selected policy to all compared systems.
protocol.case_selection: Outcome-selected highlight: require NanoJev and Jev to survive the complete 256-step horizon while the original Qwen run becomes trapped; among eligible cases prefer the largest minimum NanoJev/Jev food score, then their mean food score.
protocol.maze_selection: Fixed existing 50x50 OOD case; deterministic model-guided local-edge exploration, not stochastic action sampling.
protocol.common_snake_code: Filter immediate collisions; retain actions on shortest static safe food paths when available; model ranks remaining ties; forced moves use code.
protocol.original_case_selection: Among shared cases in the selected policy, maximize minimum NanoJev/Jev food score, then their mean food score, then the food-score gap above the native baseline. Preserve complete recorded episodes and label the result as a selected showcase, not a cohort average.

selection_revision.timing: After examining greedy outcomes; this is an editorial showcase selection, not a preregistered model-quality estimate.
selection_revision.reason: The user requested the most interesting complete game example and previously specified successful NanoJev/Jev runs with a failing untuned baseline. All eight-case controller results remain in the comparison summary.

selection_protocol.verification_scope: The supplied winner and complete selected traces are replayed. This builder does not independently rerun or select among alternate controllers.

frame_semantics: Frame zero is initial state. Every subsequent frame follows one actual attempt, including collisions and the final outcome. Probabilities describe the decision that produced that frame. done marks playback completion, including a live Snake at horizon or trapped, not necessarily a full-board win.
playback: Environment-step playback; not a model latency race.
selection_scope: Selected showcase cases and controllers; not an unbiased benchmark subset.
